name: NDA & NA
fullName: UPSC National Defence Academy and Naval Academy Examination
nameHi: राष्ट्रीय रक्षा अकादमी एवं नौसेना अकादमी परीक्षा
frequency: Twice a year (NDA I and NDA II)
approxCandidates: ≈4–6 lakh applicants per cycle (approx.); about 400 vacancies per cycle
eligibility: Unmarried candidates aged 16½–19½ who have passed or are appearing in Class 12; Physics, Chemistry and Maths required for the Air Force, Navy and Naval Academy wings

notification.summary: NDA & NA (II) 2026 was held on 13 September 2026, and its written result is expected in October 2026. Per UPSC's Calendar 2027, the NDA & NA (I) 2027 notification is due on 2 December 2026 and the exam on 11 April 2027. Dates are provisional; upsc.gov.in itself could not be reached from the research sandbox.

pattern.notes: There are two papers of 2½ hours each: Mathematics (120 questions × 2.5 marks) and the General Ability Test (150 questions × 4 marks; English 200 marks and GK 400 marks). Every wrong answer costs one-third of the question's marks, so the top-level 'marking' block gives the Maths values and each section carries its own 'marking'. The written test is followed by a 900-mark SSB interview. The bank holds 60 items in proportion (Maths 26, English 10, GK 24), so a short mock should be scored per section.

trendAnalysis.summary: The Maths paper is long and moderately tough. Algebra (complex numbers, quadratics, sequences, binomial, permutations and combinations) plus Calculus together give about 45% of it, and Statistics & Probability has grown recently. Time management, not concepts, is the main hurdle with 120 questions in 150 minutes. GAT English is easy to moderate and vocabulary-heavy (synonyms, antonyms, error spotting, comprehension). GAT GK is broad: Physics carries the most science weight, followed by History/Freedom Movement and Geography, with growing current-affairs and defence coverage. Overall difficulty has been stable over 2024–26, and Maths is the deciding paper.

resources.notes: UPSC posts NDA question papers on upsc.gov.in (Previous Question Papers) after each exam. Official answer keys appear only after the final result of that cycle.

pyqBlueprint.method: Built from the official NDA & NA (I) and (II) question papers that UPSC publishes, and from post-exam topic-wise analyses (Careers360, SSBCrack, Doon Defence Dreamers, Target Classes) for 2024–2025. The NDA 1 2024 maths split, for example, was about 18 algebra, 10 matrices, 11 trigonometry, 15 analytical geometry, 22 calculus with DE, 5 vectors and 19 statistics & probability, and NDA 2 2025 again stressed calculus and trigonometry. 2026 is covered from memory-based analyses and the writer's own knowledge; full analysis pages could not be fetched, and WebSearch returned only summaries. Patterns are described in our own words.

archetypes.pattern: Complex numbers: powers of i, cube roots of unity ω, modulus/argument or simplifying a quotient; distractors are ±1, ±i or ω/ω².
Quadratic equations: symmetric functions of roots (α+β, αβ, α³+β³, 1/α+1/β) or the condition for equal/real roots; trap is a sign error.
Sequences and series: nth term or sum of AP/GP/HP from two given terms; distractors from wrong index.
Permutations and combinations: arrangements of letters with repetition, digit-formation with divisibility, selections.
Binomial theorem: middle term, coefficient of x^k or term independent of x.
Sets and relations: cardinality of unions/intersections, classifying a relation as reflexive/symmetric/transitive.
Logarithms and number bases: evaluate nested logs or convert between binary and decimal.
Determinant properties: |kA|, |adj A|, skew-symmetric/singular matrices, determinant value without full expansion.
Matrix algebra: products, A² − kA, inverse, symmetric/skew-symmetric parts, Cayley–Hamilton shortcuts.
Exact values and identities: compound/multiple angles, products like sin15°cos15°, tan75° − tan15°.
Quadrant signs, trigonometric equations and principal values of inverse functions (trap: value outside principal range).
Properties of triangles (cosine/sine rule) and heights & distances.
Straight lines: distance between parallel lines, angle between lines, slope/intercept conditions.
Conics: eccentricity, foci, latus rectum of parabola/ellipse/hyperbola, circle centre and radius.
3D geometry: direction cosines, distance of a point from a plane, angle between planes/lines.
Limits and continuity: standard limits (sin x/x, (1+a/x)^x, (e^x−1)/x) and value making a function continuous.
Derivatives: chain, parametric, implicit and logarithmic differentiation.
Applications: maxima/minima, increasing/decreasing intervals, slope of tangent.
Real functions: domain, range and composition of functions.
Definite integrals using properties (odd/even, King's property ∫f(a+b−x)).
Indefinite integrals of standard forms (1/(x²+a²), substitution, by parts).
Area bounded by curves (parabola–line, circle).
Differential equations: order and degree, integrating factor, solution of variable-separable/linear equations.
Dot and cross products: perpendicularity condition, projection, area of parallelogram/triangle, |a×b|² + (a·b)².
Classical probability with dice, coins and cards (union of events, 'at least one').
Conditional probability, independent events and Bayes' theorem with two bags/urns.
Measures of central tendency and dispersion: effect of scaling/shifting on mean and variance, variance of natural numbers.
Binomial distribution parameters from mean and variance; correlation and regression coefficients.
Synonym of a word used in a sentence context; distractors include a look-alike word and an antonym.
Antonym of a word used in a sentence context; one distractor is a synonym.
Sentence split into parts (a)(b)(c) plus 'No error': subject–verb agreement traps (neither–nor, 'one of', collective nouns).
Spotting errors in prepositions, idiomatic usage, degrees of comparison or tense.
Replace the bold/underlined part (conditionals, 'senior to', subjunctive) or choose 'No improvement'.
Preposition, phrasal verb or conjunction blank in a single sentence.
Vocabulary blank: pick the contextually apt word from near-synonyms.
Arrange parts P, Q, R, S into a meaningful sentence; options are four permutations.
Short passage with a factual/inference question answered from a specific sentence.
Passage with main-idea, author's purpose or tone question.
Cloze passage: choose the word for a numbered blank (collocation/meaning).
Numerical in mechanics (kinematics, kinetic energy, projectile height) solvable in one step.
Optics and waves phenomena (twinkling, rainbow, speed of sound in media).
Electricity and magnetism: resistors in series/parallel, fuse, household circuits.
Common names and formulas of compounds (baking soda, plaster of Paris) and gases in daily use.
Physical vs chemical change, rusting, acids–bases and properties of elements.
Human physiology, nutrition and diseases (vitamins, hormones, blood groups, pathogens).
Cell and plant biology (organelles, photosynthesis).
Freedom movement events and personalities (INA, Dandi March, NCM withdrawal).
Ancient and medieval rulers and their titles/achievements.
Battles and colonial expansion (Plassey, Buxar, Panipat) and adversaries.
Indian physical geography: rivers (rift valley, west-flowing), passes, straits, boundaries.
World geography and climatology (deserts, winds, ocean features).
Earth and solar system (perihelion, International Date Line, seasons).
Constitutional articles and parts (emergency provisions, Fundamental Rights, Supreme Commander).
Elections and offices: electoral college, qualifications and age limits.
Basic economic concepts: direct/indirect taxes, inflation terms, banking basics.
Defence training institutions, ranks and equivalent ranks across services.
Bilateral/multilateral military exercises and partner countries.
Indigenous defence platforms and missiles (BrahMos, INS Vikrant, Tejas): type and developer.

questions.question: If ω is a non-real cube root of unity, then the value of (1 + ω − ω²)(1 − ω + ω²) is:
questions.explanation: Since 1 + ω + ω² = 0: 1 + ω − ω² = −ω² − ω² = −2ω² and 1 − ω + ω² = −ω − ω = −2ω. Product = 4ω³ = 4.

relevance.note: ω-product (1+ω−ω²)(1−ω+ω²)=4 is a recurring NDA item; distractors are powers of 2

questions.question: How many distinct arrangements can be made using all the letters of the word DEFENCE?
questions.explanation: DEFENCE has 7 letters with E repeated 3 times, so the count is 7!/3! = 5040/6 = 840.

relevance.note: DEFENCE arrangements (E×3) is an exact NDA letter-permutation item with 7!/2! style distractors

questions.question: The middle term in the binomial expansion of (x + 1/x)¹⁰ is:
questions.explanation: There are 11 terms, so the middle term is T₆ = ¹⁰C₅ · x⁵ · (1/x)⁵ = 252.

relevance.note: Middle term of (x+1/x)^10 = C(10,5) is classic NDA binomial

questions.question: If A = [[2, 3], [1, 4]], then det(adj A) equals:
questions.explanation: |A| = 8 − 3 = 5. For an n × n matrix, |adj A| = |A|ⁿ⁻¹, so with n = 2 the value is 5¹ = 5.

relevance.note: |adj A| = |A|^(n−1) with 25/125 traps is a faithful NDA determinant item

questions.question: If A is a square matrix of order 3 with |A| = 4, then |2A| equals:
questions.explanation: |kA| = kⁿ|A| for an n × n matrix, so |2A| = 2³ × 4 = 32.

relevance.note: |kA| = k^n|A| with 8/16 traps is NDA-standard though easy

questions.question: The value of sin 15° · cos 15° is:
questions.explanation: sin 15° cos 15° = ½ sin 30° = ½ × ½ = 1/4.

relevance.note: sin15·cos15 is explicitly an NDA-style product value

questions.question: If tan θ = 3/4 and θ lies in the third quadrant, then sin θ equals:
questions.explanation: With a 3-4-5 triangle, |sin θ| = 3/5. Sine is negative in the third quadrant, so sin θ = −3/5.

relevance.note: Third-quadrant sign trap is exactly NDA M11

questions.question: The value of tan 1° · tan 2° · tan 3° · … · tan 89° is:
questions.explanation: Pair tan θ with tan(90° − θ) = cot θ, so each pair has product 1. The middle term, tan 45°, is also 1, so the whole product is 1.

relevance.note: tan1°…tan89° product is a well-known NDA item with 0/undefined traps

questions.question: The distance between the parallel lines 3x + 4y − 7 = 0 and 6x + 8y + 6 = 0 is:
questions.explanation: Write the second line as 3x + 4y + 3 = 0. Distance = |−7 − 3| / √(3² + 4²) = 10/5 = 2.

relevance.note: Parallel lines needing coefficient normalisation is an NDA trap item

questions.question: If a line makes angles α, β and γ with the positive x, y and z axes respectively, then sin²α + sin²β + sin²γ equals:
questions.explanation: cos²α + cos²β + cos²γ = 1, so the sum of the sin² terms is 3 − 1 = 2.

relevance.note: Σsin² of direction angles = 2 is a repeated NDA item

questions.question: The value of lim(x→0) (1 − cos 2x)/x² is:
questions.explanation: 1 − cos 2x = 2 sin²x, so the limit is 2 · lim (sin x/x)² = 2.

relevance.note: (1−cos2x)/x² standard limit, NDA-type

questions.question: If y = xˣ (x > 0), then dy/dx equals:
questions.explanation: ln y = x ln x, so (1/y) dy/dx = ln x + 1 and dy/dx = xˣ(1 + ln x).

relevance.note: d/dx x^x is a staple NDA log-differentiation item

questions.question: The area of the region bounded by the curves y = x² and y = x is:
questions.explanation: The curves meet at x = 0 and x = 1, and y = x lies above. Area = ∫₀¹ (x − x²) dx = 1/2 − 1/3 = 1/6 square unit.

relevance.note: Area between y=x² and y=x is an NDA M22 classic

questions.question: The order and degree of the differential equation (d²y/dx²)³ + (dy/dx)⁴ + y = 0 are respectively:
questions.explanation: The highest derivative is d²y/dx², so the order is 2. That derivative appears to the power 3, so the degree is 3.

relevance.note: Order/degree with powered second derivative matches NDA

questions.question: For what value of λ are the vectors i + λj + 2k and 2i − j + k perpendicular?
questions.explanation: The dot product must be zero: 2 − λ + 2 = 0, so λ = 4.

relevance.note: Perpendicularity λ solve is NDA vector standard

questions.question: If |a| = 3 and |b| = 4, then |a × b|² + (a · b)² equals:
questions.explanation: |a × b|² + (a · b)² = |a|²|b|²(sin²θ + cos²θ) = 9 × 16 = 144 (Lagrange's identity).

relevance.note: |a×b|²+(a·b)² identity is a named NDA archetype

questions.question: The variance of the first 10 natural numbers is:
questions.explanation: The variance of 1, 2, …, n is (n² − 1)/12 = 99/12 = 8.25.

relevance.note: Variance of first n naturals (n²−1)/12 is an NDA favourite

questions.question:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
Neither the captain nor the soldiers (A) / was aware of (B) / the change in plan. (C) / No error (D)
questions.explanation: With 'neither … nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject. 'Soldiers' is plural, so part B should read 'were aware of'.

relevance.note: Neither-nor proximity agreement is an exact NDA error-spotting trap

questions.question:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
He is one of the best cadet (A) / that the academy (B) / has ever produced. (C) / No error (D)
questions.explanation: 'One of the best' takes a plural noun, so part A should read 'one of the best cadets'.

relevance.note: 'one of the best cadet' plural trap is classic NDA

questions.question:
Choose the best replacement for the underlined part. If none is needed, choose 'No improvement'.
'If I was the commander, I would order a retreat.' (underlined: If I was)
questions.explanation: An unreal present condition takes the subjunctive 'were': 'If I were the commander, I would …'. 'Had been' would need 'would have ordered'.

relevance.note: Subjunctive 'If I were' sentence improvement is NDA-standard

questions.question: Fill in the blank: The troops were asked to refrain ______ firing until ordered.
questions.explanation: 'Refrain' is followed by 'from'.

relevance.note: refrain from is standard NDA preposition blank

questions.question: Fill in the blank: Hardly had the train left the station ______ the alarm was raised.
questions.explanation: 'Hardly/Scarcely … when' is the correct correlative. 'No sooner' pairs with 'than'.

relevance.note: Hardly…when with 'than' trap is an NDA staple

questions.question: The twinkling of stars is mainly due to:
questions.explanation: Starlight is refracted by turbulent air layers whose refractive index keeps changing, so the apparent position and brightness of a star flicker.

relevance.note: Twinkling = atmospheric refraction is a frequent NDA GAT item

questions.question: Who proclaimed the Provisional Government of Free India (Azad Hind) at Singapore in October 1943?
questions.explanation: Subhas Chandra Bose proclaimed the Azad Hind provisional government in Singapore on 21 October 1943 and led the Indian National Army.

relevance.note: Azad Hind govt with Rash Behari distractor is NDA-style

questions.question: Who was the first and only Indian to hold the office of Governor-General of independent India?
questions.explanation: C. Rajagopalachari succeeded Lord Mountbatten in June 1948 and held the post until it was abolished on 26 January 1950.

relevance.note: Rajaji as only Indian GG is a recurring NDA fact

questions.question: Which rank in the Indian Navy is equivalent to a Colonel in the Indian Army?
questions.explanation: Colonel (Army) = Captain (Navy) = Group Captain (Air Force).

relevance.note: Navy Captain = Army Colonel equivalence is a real NDA item

questions.question: If z = (1 + i)/(1 − i), then z¹⁰⁰ equals:
questions.explanation: (1 + i)/(1 − i) = (1 + i)²/2 = 2i/2 = i. Since i⁴ = 1 and 100 is a multiple of 4, i¹⁰⁰ = 1.

relevance.note: ((1+i)/(1−i))^100 is a classic NDA complex item

questions.question: If α and β are the roots of 2x² − 3x − 5 = 0, then 1/α + 1/β equals:

relevance.note: 1/α+1/β with sign trap fits M02

questions.question: How many 4-digit numbers divisible by 5 can be formed using the digits 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 without repetition?
questions.explanation: The units digit must be 5 (0 is not available). The other three places are filled from the remaining 4 digits in 4 × 3 × 2 = 24 ways.

relevance.note: Divisible-by-5 digit formation without repetition is NDA standard

questions.question: The coefficient of x⁴ in the expansion of (1 + 2x)⁶ is:
questions.explanation: The term is ⁶C₄ (2x)⁴ = 15 × 16 x⁴ = 240x⁴.

relevance.note: Coefficient of x⁴ in (1+2x)^6 with 60/480 traps is NDA-faithful

questions.question: Let R = {(1, 1), (2, 2), (3, 3), (1, 2)} be a relation on the set {1, 2, 3}. Then R is:
options: Reflexive and transitive but not symmetric
Symmetric and transitive but not reflexive
Reflexive and symmetric but not transitive
questions.explanation: All (a, a) are present, so R is reflexive. (1, 2) is in R but (2, 1) is not, so it is not symmetric. Every chain such as (1, 1),(1, 2) or (1, 2),(2, 2) gives (1, 2), which is in R, so it is transitive.

relevance.note: Relation property classification is NDA M06 style

questions.question: The binary number 101101 written in the decimal system is:

relevance.note: Binary to decimal is an NDA staple

questions.question: The value of the determinant of the matrix [[0, 2, −3], [−2, 0, 4], [3, −4, 0]] is:
questions.explanation: The matrix is skew-symmetric (Aᵀ = −A) and of odd order 3. Then |A| = |Aᵀ| = |−A| = (−1)³|A|, so |A| = 0.

relevance.note: Odd-order skew-symmetric det = 0 is NDA trap item

questions.question: If A = [[1, 2], [3, 4]], then A² − 5A equals (I is the 2 × 2 identity matrix):
questions.explanation: A² = [[7, 10], [15, 22]] and 5A = [[5, 10], [15, 20]], so A² − 5A = [[2, 0], [0, 2]] = 2I. (This also follows from the Cayley–Hamilton theorem, since A² − 5A − 2I = 0.)

relevance.note: Cayley-Hamilton A²−5A=2I is an exact NDA shortcut item

questions.question: The value of tan 75° − tan 15° is:
questions.explanation: tan 75° = 2 + √3 and tan 15° = 2 − √3, so the difference is 2√3.

relevance.note: tan75−tan15 = 2√3 is a known NDA value item

questions.question: The principal value of sin⁻¹(sin 2π/3) is:
questions.explanation: sin 2π/3 = √3/2. The principal range of sin⁻¹ is [−π/2, π/2], and the angle there with sine √3/2 is π/3. 2π/3 lies outside the range.

relevance.note: sin⁻¹(sin 2π/3) principal range trap is exact NDA M11

questions.question: In a triangle ABC, a = 3, b = 5 and c = 7. The angle C is:

relevance.note: Cosine rule 3-5-7 triangle is NDA-typical

questions.question: The acute angle between the lines y = √3x + 5 and √3y = x + 2 is:
questions.explanation: The slopes are √3 (inclination 60°) and 1/√3 (inclination 30°), so the angle between the lines is 30°.

relevance.note: Angle between lines via inclinations is NDA standard

questions.question: The eccentricity of the hyperbola x²/16 − y²/9 = 1 is:
questions.explanation: e² = 1 + b²/a² = 1 + 9/16 = 25/16, so e = 5/4. (4/5 is the reciprocal, a common slip.)

relevance.note: Hyperbola eccentricity with 5/3 trap is NDA-typical

questions.question: The distance of the point (1, 2, 3) from the plane 2x − y + 2z + 4 = 0 is:

relevance.note: Point-plane distance is a staple NDA 3D item

questions.question: The value of lim(x→∞) (1 + 2/x)ˣ is:
questions.explanation: lim(x→∞) (1 + a/x)ˣ = eᵃ; here a = 2, so the limit is e².

relevance.note: (1+2/x)^x → e² is NDA-standard

questions.question: The function f(x) = x³ − 3x has a local maximum at:
questions.explanation: f′(x) = 3x² − 3 = 0 gives x = ±1. f″(x) = 6x is negative at x = −1, so there is a local maximum there (x = 1 gives a local minimum).

relevance.note: x³−3x local max is NDA-typical

questions.question: The value of ∫₀^(π/2) sin x/(sin x + cos x) dx is:
questions.explanation: Call it I. Replacing x by π/2 − x gives I = ∫₀^(π/2) cos x/(cos x + sin x) dx. Adding, 2I = ∫₀^(π/2) 1 dx = π/2, so I = π/4.

relevance.note: King's property sinx/(sinx+cosx) is an exact NDA M20 item

questions.question: ∫ dx/(x² + 4) equals:
questions.explanation: ∫ dx/(x² + a²) = (1/a) tan⁻¹(x/a) + C with a = 2.

relevance.note: Standard 1/(x²+a²) integral with coefficient traps is NDA

questions.question: The integrating factor of the differential equation dy/dx + y/x = x² (x > 0) is:
questions.explanation: IF = e^(∫(1/x)dx) = e^(log x) = x.

relevance.note: IF of linear DE is NDA-standard

questions.question: The area of the parallelogram whose adjacent sides are a = i + j and b = i − j + k is:

relevance.note: Parallelogram area via cross product is NDA M24

questions.question: A card is drawn at random from a well-shuffled pack of 52 cards. The probability that it is a king or a heart is:
questions.explanation: P = (4 + 13 − 1)/52 = 16/52 = 4/13. The king of hearts must not be counted twice (that error gives 17/52).

relevance.note: King-or-heart with 17/52 overlap trap is classic NDA

questions.question: Bag I contains 3 red and 2 black balls; Bag II contains 2 red and 3 black balls. A bag is chosen at random and a ball drawn from it is red. The probability that it came from Bag I is:
questions.explanation: P(red) = ½ × 3/5 + ½ × 2/5 = ½. By Bayes' theorem, P(Bag I | red) = (½ × 3/5)/(½) = 3/5.

relevance.note: Two-bag Bayes is an exact NDA M26 item

questions.question: The variance of a set of observations is 4. If each observation is multiplied by 3, the new variance is:
questions.explanation: Multiplying every observation by k multiplies the variance by k², so the new variance is 9 × 4 = 36.

relevance.note: Variance scaling ×9 with 12 trap is NDA-faithful

questions.question: For a binomial distribution, the mean is 4 and the variance is 3. The number of trials n is:
questions.explanation: np = 4 and npq = 3 give q = 3/4 and p = 1/4, so n = 4/(1/4) = 16.

relevance.note: Binomial n from mean/variance is NDA M28

questions.question:
Choose the word most nearly SAME in meaning to the word in capitals:
Given the bad weather, postponing the exercise was a PRUDENT decision.
questions.explanation: Prudent means showing good judgement and care for the future, i.e. wise.

relevance.note: Contextual synonym PRUDENT fits NDA format

questions.question:
Choose the word most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to the word in capitals:
The spokesperson's reply was deliberately AMBIGUOUS.
questions.explanation: Ambiguous means open to more than one interpretation; its opposite is clear. 'Vague' is a near-synonym.

relevance.note: Contextual antonym with synonym distractor fits NDA

questions.question:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
The quality of the rations (A) / supplied to the troops (B) / have improved considerably. (C) / No error (D)
questions.explanation: The subject is 'the quality' (singular), not 'rations', so part C should read 'has improved considerably'.

relevance.note: 'quality of rations…have' agreement is NDA-faithful

questions.question:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
He did not know (A) / how to cope up (B) / with the sudden pressure. (C) / No error (D)
questions.explanation: The correct expression is 'cope with', not 'cope up with'. The error is in part B.

relevance.note: 'cope up' idiomatic error is a known NDA item

questions.question:
Choose the best replacement for the underlined part. If none is needed, choose 'No improvement'.
'He is senior than me in service.' (underlined: senior than me)
questions.explanation: Latin comparatives such as senior, junior, superior and inferior take 'to', not 'than': 'senior to me'.

relevance.note: 'senior to' improvement is exactly named in NDA E05

questions.question: Fill in the blank: The cadets were warned to abide ______ the rules of the academy.
questions.explanation: The phrasal verb is 'abide by', meaning to comply with.

relevance.note: abide by preposition blank fits NDA

questions.question:
Arrange the parts to form a meaningful sentence:
P: before the monsoon
Q: The engineers
R: completed the bridge
S: that connects the two villages
questions.explanation: Q-R-S-P gives 'The engineers completed the bridge that connects the two villages before the monsoon.' In QRPS the clause 'that connects the two villages' would wrongly describe the monsoon.

relevance.note: PQRS with relative-clause placement is NDA-type

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the question.
'Himalayan glaciers feed rivers that sustain hundreds of millions of people downstream. In recent decades many of these glaciers have been thinning and retreating, largely because of rising temperatures. In the short run, faster melting can actually increase the flow in some rivers during summer. Over a longer period, however, as the ice reserves shrink, the same rivers may carry less water in the dry months, precisely when farmers and cities need it most. Scientists therefore argue that planning for water storage and efficient use must begin now, while the rivers are still full.'
According to the passage, why can the present increase in summer river flow be misleading?
options: It shows that the glaciers are growing
It is caused mainly by heavier monsoon rain
It comes from shrinking ice reserves and may be followed by lower dry-season flows
It proves that storing water is unnecessary
questions.explanation: The passage says faster melting raises flow only in the short run; as the ice shrinks, the rivers may carry less water in the dry months.

relevance.note: Inference RC on glacier melt fits NDA

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the question.
'Himalayan glaciers feed rivers that sustain hundreds of millions of people downstream. In recent decades many of these glaciers have been thinning and retreating, largely because of rising temperatures. In the short run, faster melting can actually increase the flow in some rivers during summer. Over a longer period, however, as the ice reserves shrink, the same rivers may carry less water in the dry months, precisely when farmers and cities need it most. Scientists therefore argue that planning for water storage and efficient use must begin now, while the rivers are still full.'
The main purpose of the passage is to:
options: describe the beauty of Himalayan rivers
argue that the glaciers will never melt completely
urge early planning for water scarcity caused by glacier loss
questions.explanation: The passage builds up to its last sentence: planning for storage and efficient use must begin now.

relevance.note: Main-purpose question fits NDA E10

questions.question: A rainbow is formed due to:
options: Diffraction of sunlight by dust particles
Refraction, dispersion and internal reflection of sunlight in raindrops
Interference of sunlight reflected from the ground
questions.explanation: Sunlight is refracted and dispersed on entering a raindrop, reflected inside it and refracted again on leaving, which separates the colours.

relevance.note: Rainbow mechanism is a recurring NDA physics item

questions.question: A fuse wire used in household circuits should have:
options: Low resistance and high melting point
High resistance and high melting point
Low resistance and low melting point
High resistance and low melting point
questions.explanation: The fuse must heat up and melt quickly when excess current flows, so it is made of a high-resistance, low-melting-point alloy.

relevance.note: Fuse wire properties is NDA-typical

questions.question: Who commanded the Rani of Jhansi Regiment of the Indian National Army?
questions.explanation: Captain Lakshmi Swaminathan (later Sahgal) led the INA's women's regiment. Usha Mehta ran the Congress Radio during Quit India.

relevance.note: Lakshmi Sahgal Rani of Jhansi Regiment is NDA-type

questions.question: Which Gupta ruler was described by the historian V.A. Smith as the 'Napoleon of India'?
questions.explanation: Smith gave this title to Samudragupta because of his extensive military campaigns recorded in the Prayag Prashasti.

relevance.note: Samudragupta 'Napoleon of India' recurs in NDA

questions.question: Which of the following rivers flows through a rift valley?
questions.explanation: The Narmada (like the Tapi) flows westward through a rift valley between the Vindhya and Satpura ranges. The others are east-flowing.

relevance.note: Narmada rift valley is a recurring NDA item

questions.question: The Zoji La pass connects:
questions.explanation: Zoji La on the Srinagar–Leh highway links the Kashmir Valley with Ladakh.

relevance.note: Zoji La Srinagar-Leh fits NDA passes

questions.question: The Earth is closest to the Sun (perihelion) in:
questions.explanation: Perihelion falls around 3 January; aphelion around 4 July. This shows that seasons are caused by the tilt of the axis, not by distance from the Sun.

relevance.note: Perihelion early January is an NDA G13 item

questions.question: The Vice-President of India is elected by an electoral college consisting of:
options: Elected members of both Houses of Parliament and of the State Legislative Assemblies
All members of both Houses of Parliament
Elected members of the Lok Sabha only
Members of the Rajya Sabha only
questions.explanation: Under Article 66, the Vice-President is elected by members of both Houses, including nominated members. State legislators take part only in the presidential election.

relevance.note: VP electoral college incl. nominated members is a real NDA trap

questions.question: Which rank in the Indian Air Force is equivalent to a Major in the Indian Army?
questions.explanation: Major = Squadron Leader = Lieutenant Commander. Flight Lieutenant equals Captain, and Wing Commander equals Lieutenant Colonel.

relevance.note: Squadron Leader = Major equivalence is NDA G17

questions.question: 'Yudh Abhyas' is a joint military exercise between India and:
questions.explanation: Yudh Abhyas is the India–US Army exercise. With Russia it is INDRA, with France Shakti and with Japan Dharma Guardian.

relevance.note: Yudh Abhyas India-US is NDA exercise style

questions.question:
In the following passage there are five numbered blanks. Read it and choose the most appropriate word for blank (1).

'Discipline is often ___(1)___ with harsh punishment, but in a well-run unit it is something quite different. It is the habit of doing the right thing even when no one is ___(2)___. A young cadet learns this not from lectures alone but from the example of those ___(3)___ him. When officers keep their word, arrive on time and share the hardships of their men, discipline grows almost ___(4)___. Where they fail to do so, no amount of drill can ___(5)___ for the loss of trust.'
questions.explanation: 'Confused with' means wrongly identified as, which fits the contrast that follows ('it is something quite different'). The other words are look-alikes with unrelated meanings.

relevance.note: 'confused with' collocation in a 5-blank military passage, as in NDA GAT cloze; con- look-alike options

questions.question:
In the following passage there are five numbered blanks. Read it and choose the most appropriate word for blank (2).

'Discipline is often ___(1)___ with harsh punishment, but in a well-run unit it is something quite different. It is the habit of doing the right thing even when no one is ___(2)___. A young cadet learns this not from lectures alone but from the example of those ___(3)___ him. When officers keep their word, arrive on time and share the hardships of their men, discipline grows almost ___(4)___. Where they fail to do so, no amount of drill can ___(5)___ for the loss of trust.'
questions.explanation: The set expression is 'even when no one is watching', meaning when there is no supervision. Staring, glancing and peeping describe ways of looking and do not fit the sense.

relevance.note: 'no one is watching' - straightforward NDA cloze blank; near-synonym seeing verbs as distractors

questions.question:
In the following passage there are five numbered blanks. Read it and choose the most appropriate word for blank (3).

'Discipline is often ___(1)___ with harsh punishment, but in a well-run unit it is something quite different. It is the habit of doing the right thing even when no one is ___(2)___. A young cadet learns this not from lectures alone but from the example of those ___(3)___ him. When officers keep their word, arrive on time and share the hardships of their men, discipline grows almost ___(4)___. Where they fail to do so, no amount of drill can ___(5)___ for the loss of trust.'
questions.explanation: The next sentence speaks of officers, so the cadet learns from 'those above him', his seniors. 'Beneath' reverses the sense, and 'against' and 'across' make no sense here.

relevance.note: 'those above him' fits; prepositions as cloze options are a bit thin vs NDA's usual vocabulary blanks

questions.question:
In the following passage there are five numbered blanks. Read it and choose the most appropriate word for blank (4).

'Discipline is often ___(1)___ with harsh punishment, but in a well-run unit it is something quite different. It is the habit of doing the right thing even when no one is ___(2)___. A young cadet learns this not from lectures alone but from the example of those ___(3)___ him. When officers keep their word, arrive on time and share the hardships of their men, discipline grows almost ___(4)___. Where they fail to do so, no amount of drill can ___(5)___ for the loss of trust.'
questions.explanation: When officers set a good example, discipline grows 'almost naturally', without force. The other options contradict the positive cause just described.

relevance.note: Adverb blank decided by tone ('grows almost naturally'); antonymous distractors as in NDA

questions.question:
In the following passage there are five numbered blanks. Read it and choose the most appropriate word for blank (5).

'Discipline is often ___(1)___ with harsh punishment, but in a well-run unit it is something quite different. It is the habit of doing the right thing even when no one is ___(2)___. A young cadet learns this not from lectures alone but from the example of those ___(3)___ him. When officers keep their word, arrive on time and share the hardships of their men, discipline grows almost ___(4)___. Where they fail to do so, no amount of drill can ___(5)___ for the loss of trust.'
questions.explanation: 'Compensate for' means make up for, which fits 'no amount of drill can compensate for the loss of trust'. 'Account for' means explain, and the others do not fit.

relevance.note: 'compensate for' vs 'account for' collocation trap - faithful NDA cloze item

questions.question:
Choose the word most nearly SAME in meaning to the word in capitals:
The general's CANDOUR during the press briefing surprised the journalists.
questions.explanation: Candour means openness and honesty in speech, i.e. frankness. 'Evasiveness' is the opposite and 'grandeur' only sounds similar.

relevance.note: Sentence-context synonym with antonym distractor 'Evasiveness' - NDA E01 exactly

questions.question:
Choose the word most nearly SAME in meaning to the word in capitals:
His ALACRITY in accepting the dangerous assignment impressed his seniors.
questions.explanation: Alacrity means brisk and cheerful readiness, i.e. eagerness. 'Reluctance' is the opposite, and 'alarm' is a look-alike.

relevance.note: ALACRITY with antonym 'Reluctance' and look-alike 'Alarm' - textbook NDA synonym

questions.question:
Choose the word most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to the word in capitals:
The colonel's instructions to the patrol were always EXPLICIT.
questions.explanation: Explicit means stated clearly and in detail; implicit means implied, not stated directly. 'Clear' is a synonym and 'exquisite' a look-alike.

relevance.note: EXPLICIT/IMPLICIT antonym with synonym 'Clear' planted and look-alike 'Exquisite'

questions.question:
Choose the word most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to the word in capitals:
The regiment's reputation was BOLSTERED by its conduct during the floods.
questions.explanation: Bolstered means supported or strengthened, so the opposite is undermined. 'Strengthened' is a synonym and 'bolted' a look-alike.

relevance.note: BOLSTERED antonym with synonym 'Strengthened' and look-alike 'Bolted' - matches E02

questions.question:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
The committee (A) / are divided in their opinions (B) / about the new training schedule. (C) / No error (D)
questions.explanation: A collective noun takes a plural verb when its members act or think as individuals. 'Divided in their opinions' shows that the members disagree, so 'are' and 'their' are correct. No error.

relevance.note: Collective noun whose members disagree ('divided in their opinions') correctly takes plural - so No error

questions.question:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
A large number of applicants (A) / was rejected (B) / at the medical examination stage. (C) / No error (D)
questions.explanation: 'A number of' means 'many' and takes a plural verb: 'were rejected'. ('The number of' would take a singular verb.)

relevance.note: 'A large number of ... were' agreement error - classic NDA spotting item

questions.question:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
Of the two routes to the camp, (A) / the army engineers found (B) / the northern one the safest. (C) / No error (D)
questions.explanation: When two things are compared, the comparative is used: 'the safer'. The superlative 'safest' needs three or more.

relevance.note: Comparative for two ('safer') - degree-of-comparison error as in NDA E04

questions.question:
Choose the best replacement for the underlined part. If none is needed, choose 'No improvement'.
'Unless you do not report by 0600 hours, you will lose your leave.' (underlined: Unless you do not report)
questions.explanation: 'Unless' already means 'if not', so adding 'not' creates a double negative. The correct form is 'Unless you report …' (or 'If you do not report …').

relevance.note: 'Unless ... not' double negative improvement - long-standing NDA/CDS staple

questions.question:
Choose the best replacement for the underlined part. If none is needed, choose 'No improvement'.
'It is high time we leave for the base.' (underlined: we leave)
questions.explanation: 'It is (high) time' is followed by the past subjunctive (simple past form) to show that the action is already due: 'It is high time we left'.

relevance.note: 'It is high time + past tense' subjunctive - exactly the E05 archetype

questions.question: Fill in the blank: The officer was accused ______ gross negligence of duty.
questions.explanation: 'Accuse' takes 'of' (accused of negligence). 'Charge' takes 'with', which makes 'with' a tempting trap.

relevance.note: 'accused of' preposition blank, standard NDA fill-in

questions.question: Fill in the blank: The commander's speech was so ______ that even the exhausted soldiers felt inspired.
questions.explanation: 'Stirring' means rousing strong feeling, which fits 'felt inspired'. 'Soporific' means sleep-inducing, 'stilted' means stiff and unnatural, and 'staid' means dull.

relevance.note: 'stirring' among s-word near-forms (soporific/stilted/staid) - good NDA vocabulary blank

questions.question:
Arrange the parts to form a meaningful sentence:
P: that the bridge would not survive
Q: The engineers warned
R: another heavy monsoon
S: unless it was strengthened immediately
questions.explanation: Q-P-R-S: 'The engineers warned that the bridge would not survive another heavy monsoon unless it was strengthened immediately.' R is the object of 'survive' and must follow P directly.

relevance.note: PQRS sentence ordering with clear clause logic; matches NDA ordering format

questions.question:
Arrange the parts to form a meaningful sentence:
P: who had trained in the desert
Q: found the mountain terrain
R: The soldiers
S: unexpectedly difficult
questions.explanation: R-P-Q-S: 'The soldiers who had trained in the desert found the mountain terrain unexpectedly difficult.' The relative clause P must come right after 'The soldiers'.

relevance.note: Relative clause placement ordering; easy but typical of NDA

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the question.
'When radar was first installed along the English coast in the late 1930s, many senior officers doubted its value. The early sets were bulky, unreliable and needed operators who could interpret faint flickers on a screen. What eventually made radar decisive was not the machine alone but the system built around it: trained observers, telephone links to control rooms, and commanders who trusted the information enough to act on it at once. A brilliant invention, the episode suggests, achieves little until people and procedures are organised to use it. The same lesson applies today to new technologies, from satellite imagery to artificial intelligence, whose promise is too often judged by the device rather than by the arrangements that surround it.'
According to the passage, what finally made radar decisive?
options: The small size and reliability of the early sets
The approval of senior officers in the 1930s
The genius of a single inventor
The trained people and communication system organised around it
questions.explanation: The passage says radar became decisive because of 'the system built around it: trained observers, telephone links to control rooms, and commanders who trusted the information'. The early sets were bulky and unreliable.

relevance.note: Factual RC answered from a specific sentence; distractors contradict passage - NDA E09

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the question.
'When radar was first installed along the English coast in the late 1930s, many senior officers doubted its value. The early sets were bulky, unreliable and needed operators who could interpret faint flickers on a screen. What eventually made radar decisive was not the machine alone but the system built around it: trained observers, telephone links to control rooms, and commanders who trusted the information enough to act on it at once. A brilliant invention, the episode suggests, achieves little until people and procedures are organised to use it. The same lesson applies today to new technologies, from satellite imagery to artificial intelligence, whose promise is too often judged by the device rather than by the arrangements that surround it.'
It can be inferred that the author would judge a new military technology mainly by:
options: how well people and procedures are organised to use it
how advanced the device itself is
how cheaply it can be manufactured
how quickly senior officers approve it
questions.explanation: The author criticises judging technology 'by the device rather than by the arrangements that surround it', so he would judge it by how well it is organised and used.

relevance.note: Inference about author's criterion drawn from last sentence; matches NDA inference style

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the question.
'When radar was first installed along the English coast in the late 1930s, many senior officers doubted its value. The early sets were bulky, unreliable and needed operators who could interpret faint flickers on a screen. What eventually made radar decisive was not the machine alone but the system built around it: trained observers, telephone links to control rooms, and commanders who trusted the information enough to act on it at once. The main purpose of the passage is to:

questions.question: A ball is thrown vertically upwards with a speed of 20 m/s. Taking g = 10 m/s², the total time for which it remains in the air and the maximum height it reaches are, respectively:
questions.explanation: Time to rise = u/g = 2 s, so the total time of flight = 4 s. Maximum height = u²/2g = 400/20 = 20 m. (2 s is only the time of ascent.)

relevance.note: Vertical throw time & height - one-step kinematics as set in NDA GAT physics

questions.question: A car starts from rest and accelerates uniformly to 72 km/h in 10 s. The distance covered in this time is:
questions.explanation: 72 km/h = 20 m/s, so a = 20/10 = 2 m/s². s = ½at² = ½ × 2 × 100 = 100 m. (360 results from forgetting to convert km/h to m/s.)

relevance.note: km/h to m/s conversion trap (360 m distractor) - typical NDA GAT numerical

questions.question: If the kinetic energy of a body increases by 44%, its linear momentum increases by:
questions.explanation: p = √(2mE), so p ∝ √E. New p = √1.44 × p = 1.2p, an increase of 20%. (22% wrongly halves 44%.)

relevance.note: p proportional to sqrt(KE) percentage trap (22% half-value distractor) - classic NDA item

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. The sky appears blue because shorter wavelengths of sunlight are scattered more by air molecules.
2. Red light is used for danger signals because it has the highest frequency in the visible spectrum and is scattered the most.
3. The Sun looks reddish at sunrise because most of the blue light is scattered away over the longer path through the atmosphere.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Red has the longest wavelength (lowest frequency) of visible light and is scattered the least, so it can be seen from far away. That is why it is used for danger signals, so statement 2 is wrong.

relevance.note: Scattering statements with false red-light frequency claim; NDA uses this statement format

questions.question: Three resistors of 6 Ω each are available. Which combination of all three gives an equivalent resistance of 9 Ω?
options: Two in series and the third in parallel with them
Two in parallel and the third in series with them
questions.explanation: Two 6 Ω in parallel = 3 Ω; adding 6 Ω in series gives 9 Ω. Series gives 18 Ω, all parallel 2 Ω, and (6 + 6) ∥ 6 = 4 Ω.

relevance.note: Series-parallel combination of equal resistors - standard NDA GAT circuit question

questions.question:
Consider the following pairs (Common name – Chemical formula):
1. Washing soda – Na₂CO₃·10H₂O
2. Bleaching powder – CaOCl₂
3. Quicklime – Ca(OH)₂
4. Gypsum – CaSO₄·2H₂O
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Quicklime is calcium oxide, CaO. Ca(OH)₂ is slaked lime. The other three pairs are correct.

relevance.note: Common name-formula pairs with quicklime/slaked lime swap trap - matches G04

questions.question:
Which of the following are chemical changes?
1. Curdling of milk
2. Dissolving sugar in water
3. Rusting of iron
4. Sublimation of camphor
5. Burning of a magnesium ribbon
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation: Curdling, rusting and burning form new substances. Dissolving sugar and the sublimation of camphor are physical changes that can be reversed.

relevance.note: Physical vs chemical change list incl. sublimation trap - NDA G05 exactly

questions.question:
Consider the following pairs (Hormone – Gland that secretes it):
1. Thyroxine – Thyroid
2. Insulin – Pancreas
3. Adrenaline – Pituitary
4. Growth hormone – Pituitary
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Adrenaline is secreted by the adrenal medulla, not the pituitary. Insulin comes from the beta cells of the islets of Langerhans in the pancreas.

relevance.note: Hormone-gland pairs with adrenaline-pituitary trap; frequent NDA biology pattern

questions.question:
Which of the following vitamins are water-soluble?
1. Vitamin A
2. Vitamin B₁₂
3. Vitamin C
4. Vitamin K
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation: The B-complex vitamins and vitamin C are water-soluble. Vitamins A, D, E and K are fat-soluble.

relevance.note: Water- vs fat-soluble vitamins, code-based options as in NDA

questions.question:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
1. Gandhi–Irwin Pact
2. Arrival of the Simon Commission in India
3. Purna Swaraj resolution at the Lahore Congress
4. Chauri Chaura incident
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation: Chauri Chaura (February 1922) → Simon Commission arrives (February 1928) → Lahore session (December 1929) → Gandhi–Irwin Pact (March 1931).

relevance.note: Chronology 1922-1928-1929-1931; NDA freedom-movement ordering format

questions.question: Which one of the following statements about the Indian National Army (INA) is NOT correct?
options: The first INA was organised under Captain Mohan Singh with Japanese support
Rash Behari Bose handed over the leadership of the movement in East Asia to Subhas Chandra Bose in 1943
Bhulabhai Desai led the defence of the INA officers at their trials
The INA trials of 1945–46 were held at the Lahore Fort
questions.explanation: The INA trials (Shah Nawaz Khan, P.K. Sahgal, G.S. Dhillon) were held at the Red Fort, Delhi. The other statements are correct.

relevance.note: INA trials held at Red Fort, not Lahore Fort; NOT-correct format fits NDA though a bit detailed

questions.question:
Consider the following pairs (Ruler – Associated with):
1. Harshavardhana – Authorship of the play Ratnavali
2. Pulakeshin II – Hathigumpha inscription
3. Kanishka – Fourth Buddhist Council
4. Ashoka – Account of the Kalinga war in Major Rock Edict XIII
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explanation: The Hathigumpha inscription belongs to Kharavela of Kalinga. Pulakeshin II is known from the Aihole inscription (composed by Ravikirti). The other pairs are correct.

relevance.note: Ruler-pairs with Hathigumpha (Kharavela) trap; Ratnavali detail slightly above NDA average

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Anglo-Mysore Wars:
1. The Second Anglo-Mysore War was ended by the Treaty of Madras.
2. The Third Anglo-Mysore War ended with the Treaty of Seringapatam, under which Tipu Sultan ceded about half his territory.
3. Tipu Sultan was killed during the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War in 1799.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: The Treaty of Madras (1769) ended the First war; the Second war ended with the Treaty of Mangalore (1784). Statements 2 (1792) and 3 (1799) are correct.

relevance.note: Treaty of Mangalore vs Madras trap; NDA asks Mysore wars but statement depth is CDS-like

questions.question:
Which of the following are tributaries of the Godavari?
1. Indravati
2. Manjira
3. Bhima
4. Pranhita
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation: The Indravati, Manjira and Pranhita join the Godavari. The Bhima is a tributary of the Krishna.

relevance.note: Godavari tributaries with Bhima (Krishna) trap - frequent NDA river question

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. Duncan Passage separates Little Andaman from Car Nicobar.
2. The Ten Degree Channel separates the Andaman group of islands from the Nicobar group.
3. The Eight Degree Channel separates Minicoy from the Maldives.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Duncan Passage lies between Rutland Island (South Andaman) and Little Andaman. Little Andaman and Car Nicobar are separated by the Ten Degree Channel.

relevance.note: Andaman channels/passages statements; Duncan Passage misplacement trap - NDA G11

questions.question:
Consider the following pairs (Local wind – Region):
1. Chinook – Eastern slopes of the Rockies
2. Foehn – Alps
3. Sirocco – Sahara towards the Mediterranean
4. Harmattan – Australia
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explanation: The Harmattan is the dry, dusty north-easterly wind of West Africa (the 'doctor' of the Guinea coast). The other three pairs are correct.

relevance.note: Local winds-region pairs with Harmattan misplaced; common NDA world geography item

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about a National Emergency under Article 352:
1. It can be proclaimed on the grounds of war, external aggression or armed rebellion.
2. The proclamation must be approved by both Houses of Parliament within one month by a special majority.
3. During such an emergency, the enforcement of the rights under Articles 20 and 21 can be suspended.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Since the 44th Amendment (1978), the rights under Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended even during an emergency. That amendment also replaced 'internal disturbance' with 'armed rebellion' and required approval within one month by a special majority.

relevance.note: Art 352 grounds/approval and Arts 20-21 non-suspension trap - matches G14 exactly

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the election of the President of India:
1. Nominated members of both Houses of Parliament take part in the election.
2. Elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of Delhi and Puducherry take part in the election.
3. Members of the State Legislative Councils take part in the election.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Under Article 54 (read with the 70th Amendment), the electoral college has only the elected members of Parliament and of the State Legislative Assemblies, including those of Delhi and Puducherry. Nominated members and members of Legislative Councils do not vote.

relevance.note: Presidential electoral college incl. Delhi/Puducherry and nominated/MLC exclusions - G15

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about government budget deficits:
1. Fiscal deficit is total expenditure minus revenue receipts and non-debt capital receipts.
2. Primary deficit is fiscal deficit minus interest payments.
3. Revenue deficit is the excess of total expenditure, including capital expenditure, over revenue receipts.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Revenue deficit is revenue expenditure minus revenue receipts and excludes capital expenditure, so statement 3 is wrong. Statements 1 and 2 are the standard definitions.

relevance.note: Deficit definitions with revenue-deficit trap; valid, slightly heavier than usual NDA economy

questions.question:
Consider the following pairs (Joint exercise – Partner country of India):
1. INDRA – Russia
2. Ajeya Warrior – Australia
3. Surya Kiran – Nepal
4. Lamitiye – Seychelles
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Ajeya Warrior is the India–United Kingdom army exercise (with Australia it is AUSTRAHIND). INDRA (Russia), Surya Kiran (Nepal) and Lamitiye (Seychelles) are correct.

relevance.note: Exercise-partner pairs; Ajeya Warrior is UK not Australia - NDA G18 pattern, current in 2026

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about indigenous defence platforms:
1. Tejas is a light combat aircraft designed by the Aeronautical Development Agency and built by HAL.
2. Prachand is a light combat helicopter built by HAL.
3. Arjun is a main battle tank developed by DRDO's Combat Vehicles Research and Development Establishment.
4. INS Arihant is an indigenous aircraft carrier.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: INS Arihant is India's first indigenous nuclear-powered ballistic missile submarine (SSBN). The indigenous aircraft carrier is INS Vikrant. The other statements are correct.

relevance.note: Indigenous platforms with INS Arihant (SSBN, not carrier) trap - NDA G19

questions.question:
Consider the following pairs (Missile – Type):
1. Astra – Beyond-visual-range air-to-air missile
2. Nag – Anti-ship cruise missile
3. Akash – Surface-to-air missile
4. Agni – Surface-to-surface ballistic missile
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Nag is a third-generation fire-and-forget anti-tank guided missile, not an anti-ship missile. The other pairs are correct.

relevance.note: Missile-type pairs with Nag anti-tank trap - very common NDA question
